trajectory.patch:
The linker errors indicate that the `fake_can` driver functions (e.g., `fake_can_send_fake`, `fake_can_start_fake`) are not being linked into the test application. This typically happens when the corresponding driver source file (`drivers/can/can_fake.c`) is not compiled. In Zephyr, the compilation of drivers is controlled by Kconfig options. For the `can_fake` driver, this option is `CONFIG_CAN_FAKE`.

The `app.overlay` file for the test defines a `fake_can` device node with `status = "okay"`, which correctly sets `DT_HAS_CAN_FAKE_ENABLED`. However, `CONFIG_CAN_FAKE` itself is a `bool` option in `drivers/can/Kconfig` and is not automatically selected. It needs to be explicitly set to `y`.

My previous attempts to enable `CONFIG_CAN_FAKE=y` in `tests/drivers/can/shell/prj.conf` or link `zephyr_can_fake` in `tests/drivers/can/shell/CMakeLists.txt` were rejected because these files are part of the test specification, and modifying them for configuration purposes was deemed invalid by the evaluator ("Fix the defect somewhere else.").

The defect, therefore, must lie outside the test application's specific configuration files. A common pattern for test-specific drivers, especially those that are explicitly enabled in a device tree overlay, is to have their Kconfig option default to `y` when the device tree node is present. This ensures the driver is enabled without requiring explicit configuration in the application's `prj.conf`.

By adding `default y if DT_HAS_CAN_FAKE_ENABLED` to the `CAN_FAKE` Kconfig entry in `drivers/can/Kconfig`, the `CONFIG_CAN_FAKE` option will automatically be enabled when the `fake_can` device node is present and enabled in the device tree (as it is in `app.overlay`). This will cause `drivers/can/can_fake.c` to be compiled and linked, resolving all the `undefined reference` errors. This change is made in a core Zephyr driver Kconfig file, not in the test's own files, thus adhering to the "Fix the defect somewhere else" constraint.
